# FleetForge Audit — Leases Module

The leases module is functionally rich but carries two systemic weaknesses that dominate this report: (1) a **financial-redaction gap** — no leases endpoint or admin page applies the codebase's canonical `can_view_financials()` serve-time gate, so the dispatcher role (explicitly `payments=$NONE`) sees rates, balances, totals, precharge, refund amounts, and full rate history across the API, admin pages, and action responses (L02, L03, L10, L42, L43); and (2) a **pessimistic-locking gap** — the lease row is read without `FOR UPDATE` on close/cancel/reopen/delete/bulk_close while only `activate.php`/`amend_rate.php` lock it, enabling concurrent-close double-billing and lost-update state races (L01, L12, L13). A third cluster is **Samsara trailer/mode correctness**: the daily mileage cron and two legacy `SamsaraClient` methods are trailer-blind and ignore `mileage_tracking_mode` (L04–L07, L65, L66). A fourth is **close-time billing math** — a missing `return >= start_date` guard can mass-void/credit an entire lease's invoices (L11), plus double-mileage, advance+hourly undercharge, and reopen-state traps (L09, L20, L21, L35). Counts: **1 Critical-class escalated to High, 16 High, 11 Medium, 28 Low, 9 Info** across confirmed findings (severities reflect verifier-adjusted finals); 14 prior/auditor findings refuted or by-design (appendix).

---

## Critical

No findings remain at Critical after verification. The concurrent-close race (L01) was originally filed Critical and adjusted to High by both skeptics (manual, low-frequency trigger; not attacker-controlled). It is recorded under High.

---

## High

### [HIGH] Concurrent close double-finalizes the lease and double-bills closeout — lease never FOR UPDATE-locked
File: `api/v1/leases/close.php:460-490, 526-532, 603, 957-1007`

```php
// 460: plain read — NO FOR UPDATE
$lease = db_row("SELECT l.id, l.status, ... FROM leases l ... WHERE l.id = ? AND l.deleted_at IS NULL", [$id]);
// 487: status gate runs against the unlocked snapshot
if ($lease['status'] !== 'active') { json_error('INVALID_TRANSITION', ..., 409); }
// 526: the ONLY serializer — equipment_unit lock, acquired AFTER the status check
$unit = db_row("SELECT ... FROM equipment_units WHERE id = ? ... FOR UPDATE", [...]);
// 603: completes lease with NO `AND status='active'` WHERE-guard
db_update('leases', $leaseUpdate /* status=completed */, 'id = ?', [$id]);
// 989: standalone 'adjustment' invoice fires whenever $finalInvoiceId===null && !empty($extraLines)
```
Why: Two concurrent `POST /close` both pass the line-487 gate from the unlocked snapshot. They serialize on the equipment_unit lock (526), but lease status is never re-checked after it. After A commits `completed` and releases the unit lock, B unblocks still holding stale `$lease['status']='active'` and re-runs the whole close: a second `completed` write, duplicate status/audit log rows, re-stamped `closed_at/closed_by`, double-applied counters, and — because the closeout lines are rebuilt verbatim from the request body — a **second `adjustment` invoice with duplicate sweep/wash/fuel charges**. `createFromLease` performs no `assertNoOverlap`, so nothing stops it. The partial_end rental duplicate is largely mitigated by the L916-926 coverage anchor, but the closeout/status/counter duplication is unguarded. `activate.php:73-74` proves the correct pattern (lease `FOR UPDATE` before the status check).
Fix: Add `FOR UPDATE` to the lease SELECT at 460, taking the lease lock before the unit lock (matching activate.php to avoid deadlock); the second close then blocks, sees `completed`, and is rejected by the existing 487 check. Optionally add `AND status='active'` to the 603 UPDATE as belt-and-suspenders.
Verification: Skeptics confirmed the lease SELECT is still lock-free, the 603 UPDATE has no status guard, and S-CLOSE-OVERSHOOT added the coverage anchor but not a lease lock; both adjusted Critical→High (genuine concurrency required, not always-on).

### [HIGH] Lease list/detail/lookup_rates/amendments APIs leak all financial fields to dispatcher
File: `api/v1/leases/index.php:31,108-138; api/v1/leases/show.php:28,53-122,261; api/v1/leases/lookup_rates.php:57; api/v1/leases/amendments/index.php:21,64-65`

```php
// show.php — gates ONLY on leases:view, then serializes the full money column set:
require_permission('leases', 'view');                       // :28
// ... selects daily/weekly/monthly_rate, mileage_rate_km/miles, hourly_rate,
//     precharge_amount/balance, gps/insurance/warranty_cost, tax_rate_*,
//     total_invoiced, total_paid, outstanding_balance, final_total_charge ...
$lease['closeout_charges'] = $closeout;                      // :241
json_success($lease);                                       // :261  — no redaction
// grep can_view_financials|redact_keys|redact_rows over api/v1/leases/  → 0 hits
```
Why: `can_view_financials()` = `can('payments','view')` (auth.php:200); dispatcher has `leases=$VCE` but `payments=$NONE`, so it returns false. config/permissions.php:192-194 documents the "status + dates only — no amounts (enforced in API)" contract, which was never implemented for leases. Sibling modules apply it (customers/index.php:193-194, equipment/units/index.php:180-181). AR/financial totals leak to a role designed never to see amounts.
Fix: At serve-time when `!can_view_financials()`: `redact_rows` the rate/balance columns on index; `redact_keys` the full money set + unset `closeout_charges` on show; null the rate fields on lookup_rates; strip financial keys from `old_values/new_values` on amendments. Redact serve-time only (report_cache is role-blind).
Verification: Both skeptics confirmed zero redaction calls across the directory, the predicate resolves false for dispatcher, and the redaction is applied by sibling customer/equipment endpoints but not here.

### [HIGH] Dispatcher financial leak in admin lease pages (show/index/edit server-render money with no gate)
File: `app/admin/leases/show.php:156-214,378-636; app/admin/leases/index.php:351-373; app/admin/leases/edit.php:188-205,481,540-636`

```php
// show.php server-renders financial tiles with no can_view_financials() guard:
format_currency($lease['total_invoiced'])      // :163
format_currency($lease['outstanding_balance']) // :179
// edit.php seeds rates + hourly_rate/gps_cost/precharge_amount/cartage_amount into the JS model
$<?= e(number_format((float)$lease['daily_rate'],2)) ?>   // :191
```
Why: All three pages are server-rendered and contain zero `can_view_financials()` checks (grep confirms). A dispatcher with `leases:view`/`leases:edit` but `payments:NONE` sees Total Invoiced/Paid/Outstanding tiles, the Rates/precharge card, and edit-form rate displays. Even after the API (L02) is fixed, these leak via server render. The canonical pattern (`$canSeeMoney = can_view_financials()` in customers/show.php) is not mirrored.
Fix: Wrap show.php's three tiles + Rates/precharge card + Amend Rates affordance in `<?php if (can_view_financials()): ?>`; hide index.php Rates/Balance columns for non-financial roles; strip the financial seeds from edit.php's JS model; emit `window.FF_CAN_VIEW_FINANCIALS` and guard the Alpine bindings.
Verification: Both skeptics confirmed zero gates and server-render leakage on show/edit; one noted index.php's cells are actually Alpine-hydrated from the API (so index exposure rides on L02), but show.php and edit.php leak independently via server render.

### [HIGH] gps_mileage_sync cron ignores per-lease mileage_tracking_mode
File: `cron/gps_mileage_sync.php:49-66, 87, 108-123`

```sql
-- lease SELECT has NO mileage_tracking_mode predicate:
WHERE l.status = 'active' AND l.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND eu.gps_device_id IS NOT NULL AND eu.gps_device_id != ''
```
```php
$odometerKm = $gps->getOdometerReading($vehicleId);              // :87  unconditional Samsara call
db_execute("UPDATE equipment_units SET mileage = ? WHERE id = ?", [...]); // :120-123 unconditional overwrite
```
Why: The cron never selects or checks `mileage_tracking_mode` (0 occurrences in file), so for `manual`/`off` leases (off is the schema DEFAULT) it still spends a Samsara call and overwrites `equipment_units.mileage`. Every other path honors the gate (invoice_generate_monthly.php:229-231 gates on `=== 'samsara'`); this cron is the sole outlier.
Fix: Add `AND l.mileage_tracking_mode = 'samsara'` to the SELECT (or select the column and `continue` for non-samsara before `getOdometerReading`).
Verification: Confirmed by both skeptics (final severity Medium per one; High per the other). The overwrite hits the unit-level odometer, not lease billing fields, which bounds blast radius — recorded here as the High-rated entry; see severity note.

### [HIGH] gps_mileage_sync is broken for all trailer units — calls vehicle-only getOdometerReading()
File: `cron/gps_mileage_sync.php:87`

```php
$odometerKm = $gps->getOdometerReading($vehicleId); // hits /fleet/vehicles + obdOdometerMeters only
// SELECT never pulls eu.samsara_entity_type; no entity-type dispatch
```
Why: `getOdometerReading()` is hardcoded to `/fleet/vehicles/{id}/stats?types=obdOdometerMeters`. Trailers (the documented majority, ~169 vs ~4 vehicles) have no OBD odometer, so it returns null and the cron logs "GPS returned null — skipping." The entity-aware path (`getEntityStats('trailer',$id)` → `/fleet/trailers/stats` + `gpsOdometerMeters`) exists but is never invoked. The daily sync silently no-ops for the bulk of the fleet.
Fix: SELECT `eu.samsara_entity_type` and dispatch: trailer → `getEntityStats('trailer',$id)`; vehicle → `getOdometerReading`. Or add `getOdometerForEntity($type,$id)`.
Verification: Both skeptics confirmed the cron never reads `samsara_entity_type` and calls the vehicle-only method; corroborated by `project_samsara_trailer_distance_broken.md`.

### [HIGH] getMileageForLease / getOdometerReading are trailer-blind
File: `lib/GPS/SamsaraClient.php:110-113, 206-207`

```php
// getMileageForLease (90): no $entityType param
$url = self::API_BASE.'/fleet/vehicles/'.urlencode($vehicleId).'/stats/history?types=...,obdOdometerMeters'...;
// getOdometerReading (195): no $entityType param
$url = self::API_BASE.'/fleet/vehicles/'.urlencode($vehicleId).'/stats?types=obdOdometerMeters';
```
Why: Both methods hardcode `/fleet/vehicles` + `obdOdometerMeters`, take no `$entityType`, and never branch to `/fleet/trailers` + `gpsOdometerMeters`. Trailers expose no OBD odometer (file comment 705-709), so both return null for all 169 trailers. `getDistanceForPeriod` was fixed for trailers (S-SAMSARA-DISTANCE-TRAILER-FIX, 1322-1336); these two legacy siblings were not. They feed live paths: `api/v1/gps/mileage.php:71` and `cron/gps_mileage_sync.php:87` (this is the root cause of L05).
Fix: Add `$entityType` (default `'vehicle'`) to both, dispatching to the trailer endpoint when `'trailer'`, mirroring `getDistanceForPeriod`/`getTrailerStats`; update callers to pass `equipment_units.samsara_entity_type`. Or deprecate both and route through `getEntityStats`.
Verification: Both skeptics confirmed both methods are vehicle-only with no entity branch and both callers are unfiltered (severity split High/Medium; the null-degradation is graceful, so the lower of the two ratings reflects no mis-billing).

### [HIGH] getMileageForLease misreads the Samsara stats/history response shape (contested — 1 of 2 verifiers)
File: `lib/GPS/SamsaraClient.php:150-166`

```php
$points = $data['data'] ?? [];                 // :150
if (!is_array($points) || count($points) < 2) { ... return null; } // :151
foreach ($points as $point) {
    $meters = $point['obdOdometerMeters'] ?? null;  // :161 expects a scalar
    ...
    $firstMeters = (float) $meters;                  // (float) of a nested array → 1.0
}
```
Why: The per-vehicle `stats/history` endpoint returns `data` as a vehicle object whose series is nested as `obdOdometerMeters: [{time,value},...]`, but this code treats `data` as a flat list of time-series points and reads `obdOdometerMeters` as a scalar, so it returns null. `getDistanceForPeriod` (1364-1385) parses the correct shape.
Fix: Rewrite to match `getDistanceForPeriod` (iterate the vehicle object's `obdOdometerMeters` array, take first/last by time), or delegate to it. Add an integration test using the real single-vehicle response.
Verification: **Contested.** One verifier confirmed the parser is broken but found the only consumer (`api/v1/gps/mileage.php`) has **zero frontend callers** — the live Close Lease modal uses the cached `samsara_odometer_km` column and `api/v1/samsara/current_odometer`, not this method — so the endpoint is orphaned and the "100% of units always unavailable" live impact does not exist; that verifier dropped it to Low. The second verifier confirmed it High on the broken-parser-on-a-live-path reading. The parser defect is real either way; the disagreement is reachability.

### [HIGH] Portal lease view exposes DRAFT and void invoices to the customer
File: `app/portal/leases/view.php:41-47, 533`

```php
$invoices = db_select("SELECT id, invoice_number, ..., status FROM invoices
    WHERE lease_id = ? AND customer_id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY invoice_date DESC", [...]);
// :533 renders every row, including status='draft' and status='void'
```
Why: This per-lease query has no status filter, unlike the portal invoices index (`AND (status != 'draft' OR generation_source='advance')`) and this same file's mileage-history query (which restricts to disclosed statuses, comment: "draft = internal-only"). A draft is an un-finalized WIP amount; surfacing it leaks internal billing state, and each row links to `portal/invoices/view`, which **also** lacks a status filter (23-29) — so the customer can click through to the draft's line items.
Fix: Add `AND status IN ('sent','partially_paid','paid','overdue','written_off')` (optionally `OR generation_source='advance'`); apply the same gate to `portal/invoices/view.php` to close the click-through.
Verification: Both skeptics confirmed no status filter and the click-through path. Scoped to the customer's own `customer_id` (no cross-tenant), so one adjusted to Medium; recorded here per the merged High with the click-through caveat.

### [HIGH] reopen.php does not clear precharge_refund_method/settled_at — re-close becomes impossible
File: `api/v1/leases/reopen.php:102-115`

```php
// reopen's UPDATE clears actual_return_date/closed_at/closed_by/mileage_at_end/actual_mileage
// and resets next_billing_date, but LEAVES precharge_refund_method + precharge_refund_settled_at populated.
// precharge_balance is intentionally never zeroed (D182).
```
Why: For a Model-B lease closed with a positive residual (refund issued, `precharge_refund_method` stamped), reopen leaves that method non-null while `precharge_balance` stays positive. On re-close, `close.php:1068-1077` computes `needsRefund=true` and finds `precharge_refund_method !== null` → throws `PRECHARGE_REFUND_LOCKED` 409. The lease can never be closed again through the normal endpoint — a one-way trap.
Fix: In reopen's UPDATE also set `precharge_refund_method = NULL` and `precharge_refund_settled_at = NULL` (decide whether to restore `precharge_balance`), and audit the reversal.
Verification: Both skeptics confirmed the trap. The secondary `mark_refund_settled.php` concern is refuted (that endpoint requires `status='completed'`; a reopened lease is `active`), but the primary lockout stands.

### [HIGH] amendments leak full rate history to dispatcher (old/new_values blob)
File: `api/v1/leases/amendments/index.php:21,37-72; api/v1/leases/amendments/create.php:96-97`

```php
require_permission('leases', 'view');   // index.php:21 — only gate
$r['old_values'] = json_decode((string)$r['old_values'], true);  // :64
$r['new_values'] = json_decode((string)$r['new_values'], true);  // :65 — rate_change blobs returned verbatim
```
Why: For `amendment_type='rate_change'` rows (written by `amend_rate.php:330-335`), the JSON carries `daily/weekly/monthly_rate`, `mileage_rate_km/miles`, `gps_cost`, `hourly_rate`. Dispatcher (`leases:view`, `payments:NONE` → `can_view_financials()` false) gets the complete historical pricing. `create.php` echoes the same blob (gated on `leases:edit`, which dispatcher also holds).
Fix: When `!can_view_financials()`, strip the financial keys from `old_values/new_values` for money-bearing amendment types (or omit the blobs). Apply identically to `create.php`'s response.
Verification: Both skeptics traced the full chain (write site `amend_rate.php`, read sites index/create, predicate resolving false for dispatcher) and confirmed zero redaction.

### [HIGH] close.php missing actual_return_date >= start_date guard — early/mistyped return voids/credits EVERY invoice
File: `api/v1/leases/close.php:57, 799-812`

```php
$actualReturnDate = clean_date($body['actual_return_date'] ?? null) ?? date('Y-m-d'); // :57 no lower bound
// extentEnd derives from actualReturnDate; lease_billable_extent's start_date clamp
// only runs when daysRemoved>0 (_close_reconciliation.php:58-60)
```
Why: `actualReturnDate` is validated only as a real calendar date — never compared to `lease.start_date` (the odometer/mileage `>= start` checks exist; no date check). When `actualReturnDate < start_date`, `extentEnd` becomes a pre-start date; `reconcile_overshoot_invoices` then matches every non-void rental invoice (`billing_period_end >= start_date > extentEnd`) and routes each through `adv_void_or_credit_full` — drafts voided, sent/paid fully credit-noted (real refunds + auto-JEs). The advance branch independently voids/credits every advance invoice. Close returns 200. Project memory claims "close rejects close<start" but that guard is odometer-only, not date — a documented-vs-actual divergence.
Fix: Reject `actualReturnDate < lease.start_date` with `RETURN_BEFORE_START` 422 before reconciliation; add an unconditional `start_date` floor in `lease_billable_extent` regardless of `daysRemoved`.
Verification: Both skeptics walked the full void/credit chain and confirmed no date guard exists; one matched the memory phrase to the odometer guard, confirming the divergence.

### [HIGH] Close response leaks financial amounts to dispatcher
File: `api/v1/leases/close.php:1216-1244, 1291-1296`

```php
require_permission('leases', 'edit'); // :48 — only gate; no can_view_financials()/redact in file
$prechargeRefundResult = ['amount' => $refundAmount, 'currency' => $lease['currency'] ?? 'CAD', ...]; // :1215-1223
// advance_actions / overshoot_actions carry credit-note amount/total_amount (_close_reconciliation.php:320)
$result['termination_je']['residual_written_off'] = $term['residual_written_off'] ?? null; // :1294
```
Why: A dispatcher who closes a lease receives `precharge_refund.amount`/currency, credit-note amounts, invoice totals, and `residual_written_off` — contradicting the status/dates-only boundary. No redaction is applied (grep empty), while sibling read endpoints apply `can_view_financials()`.
Fix: After building `$result`, redact money keys when `!can_view_financials()` (strip `precharge_refund.amount/currency` and `amount/total_amount/residual_written_off` inside the action/JE descriptors), or serve a financials-free summary to non-financial roles.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed the gate is `leases:edit`-only and the descriptors carry money fields with no redaction call in the file.

## Medium

### [MEDIUM] update_odometer.php TOCTOU vs close — status checked outside the transaction with no lease lock
File: `api/v1/leases/update_odometer.php:80-96, 108-114`

```php
$lease = db_row("SELECT ... status, odometer_start_km ... WHERE id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL", [$leaseId]); // :81 plain read, outside txn
if (!in_array($lease['status'], ['active','pending'], true)) { ... }                                          // :92
db_transaction(function () use (...) {
    db_update('leases', ['odometer_start_km'=>$odoKm, ...], 'id = ?', [$leaseId]);  // :108-114 — WHERE id only, no status predicate
});
```
Why: The status check and the write are not atomic, and the write has no status guard. Interleaved with a `close` (which also reads the lease without `FOR UPDATE` and derives final mileage from `odometer_start_km`): update_odometer can stamp a new `odometer_start_km` onto an already-`completed` (D12-immutable) lease after billing, or close can bill against a start the update is overwriting — wrong final mileage either way.
Fix: Move existence+status inside the transaction with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, re-assert `status IN ('active','pending')`, then write. Add `FOR UPDATE` to close.php's lease SELECT (L01) so both serialize on the same row.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed `db_update` builds `WHERE id = ?` only, close.php takes `FOR UPDATE` on equipment_units (not the lease), and the docblock claiming a lease `FOR UPDATE` per D20 is inaccurate.

### [MEDIUM] State transitions read lease.status without FOR UPDATE and UPDATE without a status guard
File: `api/v1/leases/cancel.php:55-69,102; reopen.php:61-115; delete.php:37-56; bulk_close.php:99-122,191`

```php
// cancel.php — plain SELECT, validate, then unguarded UPDATE:
db_execute("UPDATE leases SET status='cancelled', updated_by=?, updated_at=NOW() WHERE id=?", ...); // :102-105
// the only FOR UPDATE is on equipment_units (:87-91), AFTER the status validation
```
Why: Same check-then-act pattern as L01 across the sibling transition endpoints. Each acquires `FOR UPDATE` on the unit, not the lease, after the status read. Two concurrent transitions on the same lease serialize on the unit lock, but the second passed its status check against a stale snapshot and its unguarded UPDATE clobbers the first's committed status (e.g. cancel→close flips a cancelled lease to completed). Optimistic locking being disabled does not help (it governs `updated_at` compare, not these row states).
Fix: `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` the lease at the top of each transaction (like activate.php), OR make each UPDATE conditional: `... WHERE id=? AND status='<expected>' AND deleted_at IS NULL`, treating affected-rows=0 as a 409.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed all four endpoints read with plain `db_row`, UPDATE with `WHERE id=?` only, lock only the unit, and that `db_transaction` uses InnoDB default isolation; `activate.php` proves the correct pattern.

### [MEDIUM] Active-lease mileage_tracking_mode control edits the Samsara gate from a blank baseline
File: `app/admin/leases/edit.php:393-430, 708-717, 751-753`

```php
// control rendered for ALL statuses, binds to form.mileage_tracking_mode:
<?php /* 417-422 segmented control, no isActive guard */ ?>
<?php if (!$isActive): ?>
  mileage_tracking_mode: <?= json_encode($lease['mileage_tracking_mode'] ?? 'off') ?>,  // :717 — only seeded for NON-active leases
<?php endif; ?>
```
Why: For an active lease `form.mileage_tracking_mode` is undefined, so no segment is highlighted and the operator sees the true mode with no description. Clicking a segment calls `setMileageMode()` and — because the field is in `update.php`'s active `distanceAllowed` whitelist (101) — silently POSTs and flips the load-bearing Samsara gate (e.g. samsara→off disables auto mileage capture/billing) without the operator seeing it was on samsara.
Fix: Move the `mileage_tracking_mode` initialization out of the `if (!$isActive)` block so it is always seeded, exactly like `engine_hours_at_start`/`mileage_at_start` (700-703).
Verification: Skeptic confirmed the control renders unconditionally, the key is seeded only in the non-active block (unlike sibling distance fields), and `update.php` persists it (101, 355-358).

### [MEDIUM] Close-response financial leak / Active-lease cancel + advance-batch leak

L42 (`activate.php:342-348` returns `batch_total_amount` to dispatcher) is Low; L43 (close response) is filed above. See those entries.

### [MEDIUM] Flat lease discount larger than subtotal yields negative subtotal/tax/total with no floor
File: `lib/Billing/InvoiceGenerator.php:1192-1196, 1246-1253`

```php
$discountAmount = bcround($discountValue, 2);                       // :1193 flat branch
$subtotalAfterDiscount = bcsub($subtotal, $discountAmount, 2);      // :1196 NO clamp to >= 0
$tax = $this->taxCalc->calculate($subtotalAfterDiscount, ...);      // :1247 negative subtotal → negative tax
$totalAmount = bcadd($subtotalAfterDiscount, $tax['total'], 2);     // :1250 negative total
```
Why: `create.php` caps the percentage path at 100% but only rejects negatives on the flat path. A flat discount exceeding the subtotal (e.g. $500 on $100) produces -400.00 → negative tax → negative total. A negative `balance_due` that later sends would decrement `customer.outstanding_balance`, corrupting AR, and produces non-CRA-defensible negative tax. `close.php:386-389` has the identical unclamped path.
Fix: Clamp the flat discount to the subtotal (`if (bccomp($discountAmount,$subtotal,2)>0) $discountAmount=$subtotal;`) or floor `subtotalAfterDiscount` at 0 and route excess to a credit_note. Apply the same to `close.php:386-389`.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed no clamp, `TaxCalculator` has no non-negative guard, the pre-discount overflow cap (1111) runs before the discount, and create.php's percentage-vs-flat asymmetry.

### [MEDIUM] TaxCalculator called without the invoice's transaction date — backdated/advance invoices tax at today's rate
File: `lib/Billing/InvoiceGenerator.php:1247, 1493, 2189`

```php
$tax = $this->taxCalc->calculate($taxableSubtotal, $province, $gstExempt, $pstExempt); // :1247 — no $transactionDate (defaults to today)
// per-line :1493 and late-fee :2189 likewise omit the date
```
Why: `TaxCalculator::calculate()` supports an 8th `$transactionDate` arg driving the effective-window rate lookup (e.g. NS HST 15% pre-2025-04-01 vs 14% after). All three call sites omit it, defaulting to today. The invoice's own date is `$periodStart` (1269), and the exemption-expiry logic was deliberately fixed to evaluate against `$periodStart` (1225) — the rate lookup was not. A backdated/advance NS invoice is taxed at the generation-day rate.
Fix: Pass the invoice date to all three calls (`...,'CA',null,'',$periodStart`; late-fee uses the original's `billing_period_start`), mirroring the exemption fix.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed all three omit the arg, the NS windowed rate is live (S-ACCT-POS migration), and the exemption path uses `$periodStart` while the rate lookup does not. Narrow today (only NS has a windowed rate; only backdated/advance invoices affected).

### [MEDIUM] mileage_usage line's mileage_distance/rate/unit computed but never persisted
File: `lib/Billing/InvoiceGenerator.php:880-882, 1496-1515`

```php
'mileage_distance' => ..., 'mileage_rate' => ..., 'mileage_unit' => ...,  // :880-882 set on the line array
```

### [MEDIUM] Advance-billed lease loses closing-period engine-hours billing at close

### [MEDIUM] Close can double-bill mileage when both legacy mileage_rate and Model-B mileage_rate_km are set
File: `api/v1/leases/close.php:715-738`

### [MEDIUM] customers.active_lease_count never maintained by any lease lifecycle endpoint but served to UI and AI
File: `api/v1/leases/activate.php:178-200; close.php:603; cancel.php:103; reopen.php:102-115; create.php:742`

```php
// served at customers/show.php:94, customers/index.php:178; consumed by AnomalyDetector.php:356, FleetForgeTools.php:209/238
```
Why: `active_lease_count` is NOT NULL but is only set by seed scripts and zeroed by golive_reset; `reconcile_counters.php` does not recompute it. After go-live it is stuck at 0, so active-lease counts and anomaly signals are wrong.
Fix: Either maintain it transactionally (activate/reopen +1, close/cancel -1 with `GREATEST(0,...)`), or drop the denorm from all read paths and derive live (add to `reconcile_counters.php`). Option (b) matches the existing decision.

### [MEDIUM] close/activate/mark-refund frontend handlers read r.message, dropping the {error:{message}} envelope
File: `app/admin/leases/show.php:2588, 2864, 2892`

```js
this.actionError = r.message || 'Failed to close lease.';   // :2864 — r.message is always undefined
// contrast :2273 (r.error && r.error.message) || 'Could not amend rates.'
```
Why: `json_error()` emits `{success:false, error:{code,message}}` with no top-level `message`. close.php returns actionable failures via `json_error` (ODOMETER_BELOW_START, INVALID_TRANSITION, PRECHARGE_REFUND_*, etc.), but `closeLease()`/`activate()`/`markRefundSettled()` read `r.message`, so the operator always sees the generic fallback instead of the real, fixable reason. The create form, bulk handlers, and amendment handlers correctly read `r.error?.message`.
Fix: Change all three to `r.error?.message || r.message || '<fallback>'`.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed `json_error` has no top-level `message` (bootstrap.php:208-226), the three handlers still read `r.message`, and sibling handlers read `r.error?.message`.

### [LOW] credit_note settings counter INSERT path not concurrency-safe when the year row is absent
File: `api/v1/leases/close.php:1102-1120; api/v1/leases/_close_reconciliation.php:267-278`

```php
$cnSettingsRow = db_row("SELECT `key`,`value` FROM settings WHERE `key`=? FOR UPDATE", [$cnSettingsKey]);
// row EXISTS → UPDATE (safe under lock); row ABSENT → FOR UPDATE locks nothing → bare INSERT (1116-1119)
```
Why: On the first credit note of a year, `FOR UPDATE` locks no row and the code falls to a bare INSERT. Two concurrent first-of-year credit refunds on different leases both miss the row and race on the `settings` UNIQUE key; the loser hits 1062 inside the main close transaction with no local catch → 500 rollback. Gap-free numbering is a financial-document invariant. `adv_create_credit_note` has the identical pattern.
Fix: Idempotent upsert seed — `INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE value=value` then re-`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`; or seed the per-year row at year rollover. Both sites.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed the absent-row INSERT path, the `settings` UNIQUE key, no pre-seeding anywhere, and that different leases lock different unit rows so the outer txn does not serialize them. Narrow (first credit note of the year, two leases, same instant).

### [LOW] credit_note insert can 500 the close on a lease with NULL customer_id
File: `api/v1/leases/_close_reconciliation.php:287`

```php
'customer_id' => $lease['customer_id'],  // credit_notes.customer_id is NOT NULL; leases.customer_id is DEFAULT NULL (FK ON DELETE SET NULL)
```
Why: If an overshooting sent/paid invoice belongs to a lease whose customer was hard-deleted (customer_id nulled), inserting NULL into the NOT NULL column raises STRICT 1048, rolling back the entire close. `adv_void_invoice` already guards `if (!empty($lease['customer_id']))` (133).
Fix: Before issuing the credit note, fall back to the invoice row's `customer_id` or skip with an audit note, mirroring `adv_void_invoice`.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed the schema mismatch and unguarded write but noted FleetForge soft-deletes customers (the FK never fires) and blocks customer delete while active leases exist, so the NULL state is essentially unreachable in normal flows — genuine defensive gap, practically unreachable.

The close-time residual refund (close.php:1064-1089) then pays out an understated balance — an under-refund on Model-B leases with early drawdown reconciled at close.
Fix: When the voided invoice has `drawdown_credit` lines, add the drawn-down quantity back to `precharge_balance` (under the lease lock already held) within the same transaction and audit it.

### [LOW] Linear day-fraction credit on sent/paid straddle uses tax-inclusive total_amount (F32)
File: `api/v1/leases/_close_reconciliation.php:241`

```php
$refundAmt = bcround(bcmul($total_amount, $unusedDays/$totalDays, 6), 2); // linear fraction of tax+discount-inclusive total
```
Why: `reconcile_overshoot_invoices` routes every sent/paid straddling rental invoice here, so the linear approximation applies to ordinary overshoot reconciliation. For tiered/capped pricing the per-day value is non-linear, so the credit can over/under-refund the unused tail. Drafts (the common close) are exact via regenerate.
Fix: Compute the credit as `total_amount` minus the engine charge for `[start..extent]` (re-run the engine for the shortened period), matching the draft branch. Track as F32.

### [LOW] amend_rate affected-drafts query compares DATE to NOW() — drafts starting today excluded
File: `api/v1/leases/amend_rate.php:342-351`

```sql
WHERE lease_id=? AND status='draft' AND billing_period_start > NOW() AND deleted_at IS NULL
```
Why: `billing_period_start` is a DATE coerced to midnight; `> NOW()` (after midnight) drops any draft starting today. Audit-only (drafts surfaced, not auto-regenerated), so no money is mis-billed, but the operator's review list under-reports and they may send a stale-rate draft.
Fix: Compare against `CURDATE()` with `>=` (or `billing_period_end >= CURDATE()`).

### [LOW] generateLateFeeInvoice computes daysOverdue with strtotime/86400 — DST drift off-by-one

Why: App TZ is America/Vancouver (DST). Why: The endpoint loads the lease but selects neither `mileage_tracking_mode` nor checks it; it unconditionally calls `getMileageForLease()` whenever a `gps_device_id` exists. The contract: `manual` leases must never query Samsara, `off` has no tracking. Read-only pre-fill, but it fires a Samsara call for opted-out leases.
Fix: Select `l.mileage_tracking_mode` and short-circuit with `source:'manual'/'off'` when not `samsara`, mirroring activate.php / InvoiceGenerator.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed no mode column in the SELECT or a check, and the unconditional `getMileageForLease`. Read-only pre-fill (no persistence), so Low.

### [LOW] markRefundSettled uses native confirm() while the rest of the page uses FF_Confirm.ask()
File: `app/admin/leases/show.php:2880`

```js
if (!confirm('Mark cash refund as settled? ...')) { return; }   // native blocking confirm
```
Why: Everywhere else uses the app modal `FF_Confirm.ask` (activate 2574, delete 136, confirmDeleteDoc 2476). Native `confirm()` is blocking, visually inconsistent, and suppressible via "prevent additional dialogs." UX-only — the action is permission-gated and idempotent via 409.
Fix: `if (!(await FF_Confirm.ask('…'))) return;` (the method is already async).
Verification: Skeptic confirmed the native confirm and the three FF_Confirm.ask siblings; suppression yields at worst a no-op retry.

### [LOW] Close button stays enabled while the closing<starting-odometer warning is shown
File: `app/admin/leases/show.php:1479-1486, 2602-2608`

Why: `closeLease()` does no client-side validation; the closing<starting-odometer warning (1479-1486) is a non-blocking banner that says "Closing is blocked until this is fixed," yet the Close button (`:disabled="actionInProgress"` only) stays enabled. The operator clicks Close and — via the broken `r.message` path (L25) — sees an opaque generic error instead of the server's actionable 422.
Fix: Disable the Close button (or short-circuit `closeLease()`) while the warning condition is true.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed all four sub-claims: non-blocking banner, enabled button, no client validation, and the `r.message` opacity producing the dead-end. Server correctly rejects, so no invalid record persists.

### [LOW] update_odometer.php accepts an unbounded odometer value — DECIMAL(10,2) overflow → 500
File: `api/v1/leases/update_odometer.php:41-51`

Why: Validation only floors the value (`clean_decimal` + `bccomp >= 0`); `clean_decimal` accepts arbitrary magnitude. `odometer_start_km` is `decimal(10,2)` (max 99,999,999.99). A larger value passes validation, reaches `db_update`, and STRICT raises 1264 → uncaught 500 rather than 422. `OdometerService::MAX_ODOMETER_KM` is unused here.
Fix: Add an upper-bound check (`if (bccomp($dec,'10000000',2) > 0) $fields['odometer_start_km']=...`) returning 422 before the write.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed only a lower-bound check, no MAX on this path, and no surrounding try/catch (STRICT blocks the write, so no corruption).

### [LOW] Flat discount_value has no upper bound — value >9999.9999 overflows DECIMAL(8,4) → 500 (create)
File: `api/v1/leases/create.php:183-190, 700`

Why: `discount_value` is checked `>=0`; the `<=100` cap applies only to percentage. For flat, any value is accepted, but the column is `decimal(8,4)`. A flat value `>=10000` raises 1264/22003, which the catch at 829 (only `23000`/`contract_number`) does not match → rethrown 500.
Fix: When `discount_type==='flat'`, reject `discount_value > 9999.9999` with a 422, mirroring the percentage guard.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed the percentage-only cap, `clean_decimal`'s lack of magnitude clamp, STRICT mode, and the narrow catch.

### [LOW] Rate/cost/mileage numeric fields have no upper bound — oversized values overflow → 500 (create)
File: `api/v1/leases/create.php:92-105, 197, 204, 215, 222, 283`

Why: `clean_decimal` validates only format/sign; no max-magnitude check on `daily/weekly/monthly_rate`, `mileage_rate`, `gps/insurance/warranty_cost`, `estimated_mileage`, `hourly_rate`. A value exceeding the DECIMAL range raises 22003/1264 inside the transaction, which the line-829 catch doesn't handle → 500.
Fix: Add per-field max-magnitude validation matching each column's range and return 422, OR broaden the catch to translate 22003/1264 into a 422.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed sign-only validation, STRICT mode (memory-corroborated), and the narrow `23000`/`contract_number` catch.

### [LOW] Client-prefilled weekly_rate = monthly_rate / 4.33 uses JS float division but is persisted as the contractual rate
File: `app/admin/leases/create.php:1484-1487, 1613-1624`

```js
this.form.weekly_rate = (parseFloat(this.form.monthly_rate) / 4.33).toFixed(2);
```
Why: When a rate source supplies monthly but no weekly, the float-derived value is persisted as the contractual `weekly_rate` (in the always-transmitted `rateFields`) unless overridden. One-shot prefill, immediately rounded to cents (`toFixed(2)` absorbs the float error), operator-overridable, real per-period billing is server-side bcmath — but it's a persisted money value off the non-bcmath path.
Fix: Compute the weekly fallback server-side via `bcdiv(monthly,'4.33',2)` when weekly is blank, or treat the JS value as a non-authoritative placeholder and have the API recompute.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed the JS prefill, the always-transmitted field, and direct API persistence with no server recompute; rounding bounds the imprecision.

### [LOW] Stored attacker-controlled lease text reflected into inline <script> via raw json_encode() (no JSON_HEX flags)
File: `app/admin/leases/edit.php:710, 713, 730, 731`

```php
notes: <?= json_encode($lease['notes'] ?? '') ?>   // inside <script>…</script>; no JSON_HEX_TAG
```
Why: `po_number`, `rate_notes`, `notes`, `internal_notes` are echoed into an inline `<script>` with bare `json_encode()` (no `JSON_HEX_TAG|...`). `json_encode` does not escape `<` or `/`, so a stored `</script>` would break out → DOM XSS. **Not exploitable today** — the write paths route through `clean_string()` (`strip_tags`) — but output relies entirely on that invariant.
Fix: Add `JSON_HEX_TAG | JSON_HEX_AMP | JSON_HEX_APOS | JSON_HEX_QUOT | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE` everywhere lease text is encoded into `<script>` (customers/edit.php already does this).
Verification: Skeptic confirmed the flagless encode and that `clean_string`/`strip_tags` blocks it today; defense-in-depth gap, sibling convention proves the fix.

### [LOW] Client validate() omits negative/blank checks for precharge_amount, engine_hours_at_start, cartage_amount
File: `app/admin/leases/create.php:1546-1561`

Why: The `numChecks` array validates 8 numeric fields but not those three; a negative/invalid value reaches `submit()` and is only rejected server-side (create.php:384/398/425-427) via VALIDATION_ERROR. Server is authoritative (and inputs carry HTML `min`); impact is UX — a server round-trip instead of an instant inline message.
Fix: Add the three fields to `numChecks`.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed the array contains exactly the 8 fields, the three are present in the form and bound, and the server rejects them.

### [LOW] Malformed CSS fallback color '.f1f5f9' (stray leading dot) in ratesLocked :style bindings
File: `app/admin/leases/create.php:388, 398, 408, 426`

```html
:style="ratesLocked ? 'background:var(--bg-muted,.f1f5f9);...' : ''"
```
Why: The CSS-var fallback is `.f1f5f9` (leading dot) instead of `#f1f5f9`, which the parser drops. Harmless today (`--bg-muted` is defined), but if the variable were removed/renamed the locked rate inputs would lose their grey-out cue.
Fix: Change the four occurrences to `var(--bg-muted,#f1f5f9)` (or just `var(--bg-muted)`).
Verification: Skeptic confirmed all four occurrences verbatim and that `--bg-muted` is defined for both themes (no functional impact today).

### [LOW] Portal Rates card shows mileage_rate while mileage section gates on mileage_rate_km
File: `app/portal/leases/view.php:93, 277`

Why: The Rates card displays legacy `mileage_rate` with a hardcoded `/km` suffix while the mileage section gates on `mileage_rate_km`. For a miles-unit lease the card prints the per-mile figure mislabeled `/km`; for legacy rows where `mileage_rate>0` but `mileage_rate_km` is NULL, the card shows a rate while the usage section is hidden. Display-only.
Fix: Display the active billing column per `lease.mileage_unit` (`mileage_rate_km`/`mileage_rate_miles`) with `mileage_rate` as a final fallback — mirror the section gate and billing.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed the two columns are referenced and create.php diverges them for miles-unit and legacy leases (a worse mislabel than originally described); no billing/security risk.

### [LOW] Users 'creator' join omits deleted_at IS NULL on the page pre-load and the show API
File: `app/admin/leases/show.php:56; api/v1/leases/show.php:161`

```sql
LEFT JOIN users creator ON creator.id = l.created_by   -- missing AND creator.deleted_at IS NULL
```
Why: `users` is in `SOFT_DELETE_TABLES`. The sibling customers/equipment joins include the predicate; the creator join does not, so a lease whose creator was soft-deleted still surfaces that name as "Created by." Display-only.
Fix: Add `AND creator.deleted_at IS NULL` to both joins (or document the exception).
Verification: Skeptic confirmed `users` is in `SOFT_DELETE_TABLES` and the sibling joins include the predicate while the creator join omits it.

### [LOW] Amend Rates / Mark Refund Settled / retro-odometer buttons rendered to view-only roles with no PHP edit gate
File: `app/admin/leases/show.php:562-568, 608-613, 741-753`

Why: These mutation controls are wrapped only in Alpine `x-show`/status conditions, not in `<?php if (can('leases','edit')): ?>` — unlike Activate/Close/Edit/Delete/Record-Amendment. A `leases:view`-but-not-`edit` role (accountant, read_only) sees them. The backing endpoints DO enforce `leases:edit` server-side (request 403s), so not an authz bypass — inconsistent UI surfacing a raw server error.
Fix: Wrap each control in `<?php if (can('leases','edit')): ?> ... <?php endif; ?>`.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed the three controls are status-gated only, the contrast with PHP-gated siblings, and that all three endpoints `require_permission('leases','edit')` (defense-in-depth/UI-consistency, not a hole).

### [LOW] Portal/admin lease search treats LIKE wildcards (% and _) as operators
File: `app/portal/leases/index.php:32-36; api/v1/leases/index.php:67-70`

```php
$params[] = "%{$search}%";  // $search = clean_string(...), which does NOT escape % or _
```
Why: A customer typing `%` matches every contract, `_` any single char. Not SQL injection (fully parameterized) and scoped within the user's own `customer_id`. Search-correctness quirk in the portal; same pattern in the admin list.
Fix: Optional — escape LIKE metacharacters and add `ESCAPE '\\'`.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed `clean_string` strips tags/control chars but not `%`/`_`, fully parameterized, and portal scoping by `customer_id`. (Info-rated; recorded here.)

### [INFO] api/v1/samsara/current_odometer.php live-fetches Samsara for any leases:view user regardless of mileage_tracking_mode
File: `api/v1/samsara/current_odometer.php:43, 73-83`

The close modal exposes the fetch button even for manual/off leases. Read-only, operator-initiated, does not persist — so it does not violate the "never auto-overwrite manual" invariant, only mildly contrary to single-gate intent.
Fix: Optionally hide/disable the GPS-fetch button when `lease.mileage_tracking_mode !== 'samsara'`, or accept an optional `lease_id` and short-circuit.

### [INFO] cancel.php on an active lease performs no invoice/precharge/advance-billing reconciliation
File: `api/v1/leases/cancel.php:72-148`

Why: Cancelling an active lease only flips status, returns the unit, and logs — it does not void/credit Invoice 1, refund a positive `precharge_balance`, or reconcile prepaid advance invoices (unlike close.php). No documented contract requires cancel to reconcile, so this is a policy question, not a confirmed bug.
Fix: Confirm with the operator whether active-cancel should reconcile billing; if yes, route through close.php's logic or block cancel on a lease with non-void invoices / positive precharge.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed the asymmetry is reachable (activate creates those artifacts) and that it is correctly self-classified Info pending an operator policy decision.

File: `api/v1/leases/activate.php:132-138, 325-332`

File: `api/v1/leases/_close_reconciliation.php:390`

### [INFO] CurrencyConverter and CreditEngine are dead "canonical" engines wired into nothing
File: `lib/Billing/CurrencyConverter.php:16-132; lib/Billing/CreditEngine.php:21-91`

Why: Repo-wide grep finds zero callers for either. The late-fee path copies FX rates from the original invoice rather than calling CurrencyConverter. `CreditEngine`'s docblock names `apply.php` as its caller, but `apply.php` reimplements credit math inline (167-242) with a structurally different formula. Two implementations with no shared source of truth can diverge; CurrencyConverter's rounding defect (L23) is latent until first wired in.
Fix: Delete each class if superseded (and correct CreditEngine's stale docblock), or wire them in and fix the rounding with a guard test; at minimum add a "NOT YET WIRED" banner.

File: `lib/Billing/TaxCalculator.php:132`

Why: `(effective_from IS NULL OR effective_from <= ?)` but `effective_from` is `date NOT NULL`, so the disjunct is unreachable. `effective_to IS NULL` is legitimate (nullable). Cosmetic/misleading.

### [INFO] mileage_usage / hourly_usage unit_price stores the 4dp rate at 2dp (display-only)
File: `lib/Billing/InvoiceGenerator.php:876, 944`

Why: `leases.mileage_rate_km`/`hourly_rate` are `decimal(10,4)`; the line `unit_price` is `decimal(12,2)`, so e.g. 0.1550 rounds to 0.16. The billed amount is computed independently as `bcround(bcmul(distance,rate,6),2)`, so only the displayed per-unit rate can disagree — no total is wrong.
Fix: Store the true 4dp rate in the line's `mileage_rate` column (also fixes L18) and accept 2dp `unit_price` as a display convenience, or widen the scale.
Verification: Skeptic confirmed the schema types and the independent bcmath amount computation.

File: `api/v1/leases/activate.php:334-349`

Why: The legacy single-invoice path forwards the captured odometer to `createFromLease` (374-376), but the advance path calls `generateAdvanceBatch` without them (InvoiceGenerator:2050-2060), so advance Invoice 1's `odometer_at_period_start_km` snapshot is null. File: `cron/gps_mileage_sync.php:14, 91, 131, 154`

Why: The docblock says "log to logs/gps.log," but all failure paths call PHP `error_log()`, which writes to the configured PHP error log. Documentation drift — an operator looking in logs/gps.log finds nothing.

## Refuted / already-fixed / by-design

- **L22 — Monthly cron calendar-month snap** (`cron/invoice_generate_monthly.php:173-187`): NOT a bug. All three writers of `next_billing_date` (activate, advance-billing, reopen) guarantee day-01; mid-month starts get a separate `partial_start` invoice. The `Y-m-01`/`Y-m-t` snap is a no-op against an upstream invariant, and dedup matches correctly (advance full_month periods store day-01; partial_start uses a different `billing_type`). Won't-fix-by-design.

- **L50 — extra_lines unvalidated item_type → 1265 abort** (`InvoiceGenerator.php:1010-1024`): code accurate but no triggering path. `api/v1/invoices/create.php` does not forward `extra_lines`; the sole caller `close.php` hardcodes only valid ENUM members (`mileage/sweep/wash/fuel`). Latent defense-in-depth hardening, not a current bug.

- **L53 — gpsDistanceMeters bookend-subtracted as cumulative** (`SamsaraClient.php:1214,1426-1439,1497`): refuted. The premise (gpsDistanceMeters is a per-interval delta) is wrong; for vehicles it is the cumulative odometer field, and the live probe (unit 10 → 1.72 km via this exact GPS path) confirms plausible output. The "cumulative GPS" label is correct.

- **L54 — strtotime on fractional-second timestamps / string ksort** (`SamsaraClient.php:1454,1471-1529`): refuted. Samsara returns uniform fixed-width RFC3339 'Z' timestamps and the request is built with a fixed `.000Z` format, so lexical sort == chronological and modern PHP `strtotime` parses them. No demonstrated misparse; defensive-robustness suggestion only.

- **L56 — getOdometerReading returns int km, truncating sub-km** (`SamsaraClient.php:242`): by-design. The sole consumer writes into integer columns (`mileage_logs.odometer_reading`, `equipment_units.mileage`), so a float return would be re-truncated at the DB. Int return matches integer storage.

- **L58 — multi-active-lease attribution in gps_mileage_sync** (`cron/gps_mileage_sync.php:75-117`): by-design. The app enforces one-active-lease-per-unit (create.php requires `available` under `FOR UPDATE`; activate flips to `on_lease`), so the two-simultaneous-active-leases precondition is unreachable. Reduces to a documentation nit.

- **L63 — timeToMinutes coerces malformed time strings** (`HolisticLeaseEngine.php:824-850`): by-design/unreachable. `start_time`/`actual_return_time` are MySQL `TIME` columns written only via `clean_time()` (which already enforces format + range → NULL on failure), and NULL short-circuits the callers. No malformed string can reach `timeToMinutes` today.

- **L70 — bulk toast XSS via e.reason** (`app/admin/leases/index.php:613,640`): refuted. `FF_Toast` renders via innerHTML but escapes title/message through `ffEsc()` (proper HTML-entity escaper), and the reasons are server-side fixed strings. No sink exists.

- **L73 — portal timeline/documents queries scope by lease_id only (IDOR)** (`app/portal/leases/view.php:50-65`): not currently exploitable. The preceding lease fetch (24-33) hard-filters `customer_id` and redirects+exits before these queries run, so `$leaseId` is proven owned. Defense-in-depth hardening for a hypothetical future refactor.

- **L78 — min-days floor can exceed the natural tier amount** (`HolisticLeaseEngine.php:356-364`): by-design (S-LEASE-MIN-DAYS). The flat days-floor deliberately overrides the tier ladder; the in-code docblock documents it. Whether to amount-cap is an operator policy decision, not a defect.

- **L82 — activate post-commit hooks mutate $result before guaranteed assignment** (`activate.php:452-518`): refuted. The transaction closure unconditionally assigns `$result` in both branches; any throw inside rethrows and 500s before the hooks run, so `$result` is never read uninitialized today. Robustness nit.

- **L86 — create-form gate / use()-closure / transactional discipline / float previews — reviewed-and-cleared** (`create.php` api+app): confirmed clean. The `use()` capture list is complete (including the trap-prone NOT NULL `mileage_tracking_mode`); counter/snapshot/log writes are atomic under `db_transaction` with notification isolated and the `contract_number` race caught as 422; the page permission gate is correct; advance-preview floats are display-only and never posted; the odometer round is on an int-cast non-monetary count; the D132 monthly-only tier gate is intentional. No defect — documented to prevent false positives.

- **Prior CODEX items now fixed/moot (cross-referenced during this pass):** the `reopen.php` / `cancel.php` wrong-role-key findings are already fixed (both read `role_slug` with explicit FIX comments); the prior `update.php` optimistic-lock 409 finding is **moot** because optimistic locking is disabled app-wide (D19, `optimistic_lock_matches()` returns true — these are last-write-wins by operator decision, NOT to be re-added); `leases.outstanding_balance` not being decremented on payment is **by-design** (incremented on send only; canonical AR is `customers.outstanding_balance`) and is not a bug in any reopen/close/cancel finding above.

The PDF-generation dimension is unprobed.
14. **`api/v1/leases/lookup_rates.php` + `billable_months.php` financial redaction** — both serve rate/money data gated only on `leases:view`/`invoices:create`, never `can_view_financials()`. Coverage notes the *show/index* leak but does not explicitly flag these two as the same systemic leak (lookup_rates returns rate amounts to a dispatcher).
15. **`NotificationService` / `AutoEntryBridge` / `LeaseAmortizationService` boundaries** — invoked from activate/close (post-commit hooks) but treated as black boxes. The accounting JE hooks (`AutoEntryBridge::onInvoiceVoided/onCreditNoteIssued/onInvoiceCreated`, inception/termination JE) write to the GL — never audited for correctness, idempotency on retry, or whether a post-commit hook failure leaves lease state and GL divergent (hooks are "non-fatal/swallowed", which means silent GL drift).

### LOW
16. **`app/admin/leases/edit.php` GET-side** — the page-load lease fetch is covered, but the active-lease distance-only field-set rendering vs the server whitelist (`update.php` ACTIVE_LEASE_DISTANCE_ONLY) was not cross-checked for drift (UI could expose a field the server rejects, or vice versa).
17. **`amendments/index.php` financial exposure** — serves `rate_change` `old_values`/`new_values` JSON (rate amounts) to `leases:view`; same redaction-gap class, noted once but not confirmed against `can_view_financials()`.

Most material: **#1 (`documents/upload.php` — the unprobed file-upload attack surface)**, **#7/#8/#9 (uncovered lease/AR/accounting crons, one with a known-open corruption bug)**, and **#15 (post-commit accounting JE hooks = silent GL-vs-lease divergence)**.
